clue.text: Titled man gives lad back repaired motor

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for the lad from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters of motor are reassembled

explanation.surface: A nobleman hands his boy a car engine that has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SON into NOS; 'repaired' rearranges MOTOR into TROMO. 'Titled man' is not a lord: he is the man who gives a novel its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad's novel is named after its hero, so he is literally a title character.

clue.text: Lack of call to vocation?

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation used when calling to someone, as in 'O Lord'
a vocation is a calling, a mission in life

explanation.surface: Someone feels no summons to a religious calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' is the old vocative cry used to address someone; put before MISSION it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a gap where something has been left out, hence a lack.

clue.text: Gent I outed naughtily is speechless

indicators.note: behaving naughtily suggests misbehaving letters that get jumbled

explanation.surface: A gentleman whom someone mischievously outed is lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges the letters of GENT I OUTED; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tongue-tied means being unable to get words out, so speechless.

clue.text: Pebble-dash may be free

definitions.meaning: pebble-dash is a rough coating of small stones on an exterior wall, so it is found on a building
given without charge, as a drink a landlord offers

explanation.surface: A house's pebble-dash coating might come at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: Pebble-dash is a British exterior wall finish of render studded with small stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something supplied at the establishment's expense means given free.

clue.text: Be down to embrace woman cow!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the debt word wraps around the woman

parts.note: to be down is to be in debt, to owe
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to hug a woman, followed by a rude insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' is a verb here, meaning intimidate, not the animal or an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to subdue them by fear, which is to intimidate or daunt.

clue.text: Use pressure with stick

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Push with a stick, applying force.
explanation.walkthrough: P for pressure followed by ROD for stick; the whole clue also describes the action.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke, pushing at something with a pointed stick or finger.

clue.text: Plan second church across border

indicators.note: the church letters stretch across, either side of, the border

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A plan to build a second church on the far side of a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means the church abbreviation straddles the border word. 'border' is not a frontier but the edge of a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan or arrangement for doing something.

clue.text: Put all energy into game, but caused trouble

definitions.meaning: played hard, giving one's all in a match
misbehaved, as a child or a faulty machine acts up

explanation.surface: A player tried hard in the match but was a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both playing up to one's best and acting up, misbehaving.

clue.text: Sort of take-off of the Perpendicular style

definitions.meaning: an aircraft that rises straight up makes a VTOL kind of take-off
perpendicular means at right angles to the horizontal, upright

explanation.surface: A kind of parody of the Gothic architectural style called Perpendicular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' looks like a parody and 'Perpendicular' like the English Gothic style; really they are an aircraft launch and an upright line.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright and straight up describes both a jump-jet's rise and a perpendicular line.

clue.text: Singer allowed out of hotel

indicators.note: the permission word sits on the outside of the hotel word

parts.note: to let is to allow
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A singer is let out of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' here means outside: LET goes outside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch known for its song, so a songbird.

clue.text: Managed to get in close, but badly treated

indicators.note: one piece gets in, goes inside, the other

parts.note: hard by means close by, near
done means managed or accomplished

explanation.surface: Someone got near, only to be treated unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' puts the managed word inside an old two-word phrase meaning nearby; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling hard done by means feeling one has been treated unfairly.

clue.text: Having a hundred-odd acres, so bound to be conventional?

definitions.text: Having a hundred-odd acres, so bound to be conventional?

parts.words: Having a hundred-odd acres, so bound to be conventional?
parts.note: an old English unit of land of about 120 acres which, with bound added, gives a word meaning narrow-minded and conventional

explanation.definitionFit: A hide was an old English measure of land, roughly 120 acres, enough to support a household.

clue.text: Compel to go to Surrey for book

indicators.note: to means the dispatch word is added on to the end of the name

parts.note: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, was the Tudor poet; Howard is the Surrey family name
to send is to make someone go

explanation.surface: Forcing someone to travel to Surrey for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrey' looks like the county, but stands for the Earl of Surrey, Henry Howard. HOWARDS END is E. M. Forster's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Howards End is a 1910 novel by E. M. Forster, so a book.

clue.text: Extremely reasonable request for copy

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, taking the first and last letters of reasonable

parts.note: a petition is a formal request

explanation.surface: A very reasonable request to make a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier but takes the first and last letters of 'reasonable', R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A repetition is a repeat, something done again, hence a copy.

clue.text: Needing to change, use standby suit

indicators.note: the letters of use standby need to change into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone must change and wear the spare suit kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges USE STANDBY; 'Needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunday best is one's finest clothes, worn for church, such as a good suit.

clue.text: Soldier needs one month to go round island

parts.note: a soldier is a caste of ant
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to go round means to turn about, reading the month backwards

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

explanation.surface: A soldier must spend a month travelling around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' tempts GI, but it is an insect from the soldier caste; 'to go round' turns the month abbreviation backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Powerful light may explode

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters of light may are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A strong lamp could blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explode' rearranges LIGHT MAY; 'may' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Almighty means having unlimited or great power, so very powerful.

clue.text: Sort of jam-jar — how to get at contents?

definitions.meaning: jam-jar is rhyming slang for car, and one with a roof that folds away is a convertible
to reach what is inside a jar you take off the lid, uncovering the top

explanation.surface: A kind of jam jar, and a question about how to reach the jam.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam-jar is British rhyming slang for car, so 'Sort of jam-jar' is a convertible, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-top car has no fixed roof, and an uncovered jar's top is open.

clue.text: Like, or love, article about football managers

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
the FA, the Football Association, runs English football
a piece is an article in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fan likes or loves a newspaper article about football managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'football managers' are not club managers but the FA, the body governing English football; 'or' and 'about' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of a piece are alike, consistent with one another.

clue.text: Emperor is hard on pope

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
Adrian is the name of several popes, including the English Adrian IV

explanation.surface: An emperor is tough on the pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places H above ADRIAN in this down answer. Hadrian was the Roman emperor who built the wall across northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian ruled as Roman emperor from AD 117 to 138.

clue.text: Troubled zone, as it might well be?

definitions.text: Troubled zone, as it might well be?

parts.words: Troubled zone, as it might well be?
parts.note: a region of long-running conflict; the word zone has an o in its middle and the letter e at its end

explanation.definitionFit: The region from Egypt to Iran is often described as a troubled zone of conflict.

clue.text: Imagined engineers would get through obstruction on time

indicators.note: the engineers get through, pass into the middle of, the obstruction

parts.note: a dam obstructs a river
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Engineers imagined pushing through a blockage on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would get through' puts the Royal Engineers inside the barrier, and time follows; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamt is a past form of dream, here meaning imagined or fancied.

clue.text: Not close to a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, usually of beer

explanation.surface: Someone is not near to having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is a verb, shut, not an adjective. A jar is British slang for a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, so not fully closed.

clue.text: In a commando unit one regularly goes over the top

definitions.text: In a commando unit one regularly goes over the top

parts.words: In a commando unit one regularly goes over the top
parts.note: a commando's headgear sits on the head, and the soldier also often charges over the parapet

explanation.definitionFit: The green beret is worn by Royal Marine commandos, and the name is used for the soldiers themselves.

clue.text: Concerned with losing head in fight

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: about means concerning, to do with

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about losing their head in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the A from ABOUT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing or wrestling match, so a fight.

clue.text: Climbers I cross, bringing pollinating insects round

indicators.note: the insects go round, enclosing, the cross

parts.note: bees pollinate flowers
X is a cross

explanation.surface: Climbers cross paths with bees and bring them along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts BEES around X, giving BEXES after I; 'bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibexes are wild mountain goats famed for climbing steep crags.

clue.text: Drone may be brought to arm Uboat

indicators.note: the answer may be brought to, made into, arm Uboat by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A droning aircraft could be brought up to arm a German submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be brought to' signals a rearrangement of ARM UBOAT. 'Drone' is not an aircraft but the sustained note of an Indian lute.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamboura is an Indian long-necked lute played to provide a continuous drone accompaniment.

clue.text: Matches on square often nervous for batsmen

indicators.note: on means the second word follows the first in this across entry

parts.note: nine is the square of three
ties are matches, as in cup ties

explanation.surface: Cricket matches on the square often make batsmen nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is not the cricket pitch but a square number. Batsmen nearing a century are said to be in the 'nervous nineties'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers talk of the nervous nineties, the scores just short of a hundred that make batsmen edgy.
